evidence.pali: ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu abhikkante paṭikkante sampajānakārī hoti, ālokite vilokite sampajānakārī hoti, samiñjite pasārite sampajānakārī hoti, saṅghāṭipattacīvaradhāraṇe sampajānakārī hoti, asite pīte khāyite sāyite sampajānakārī hoti, uccārapassāvakamme sampajānakārī hoti, gate ṭhite nisinne sutte jāgarite bhāsite tuṇhībhāve sampajānakārī hoti. Tassa evaṃ appamattassa ātāpino pahitattassa viharato ye gehasitā sarasaṅkappā te pahīyanti. Tesaṃ pahānā ajjhattameva cittaṃ santiṭṭhati sannisīdati ekodi hoti samādhiyati. Evampi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāyagatāsatiṃ bhāveti.
evidence.chinese_simplified: 再者，诸比丘，比丘于前进、后退时保持正知，于前视、环顾时保持正知，于屈、伸时保持正知，于持僧伽梨、钵、衣时保持正知，于食、饮、嚼、尝时保持正知，于大小便时保持正知，于行、住、坐、卧、醒、语、默时保持正知。他如是住于不放逸、热忱、策励，舍离了与居家生活相关的寻思。因舍离彼等，其心于内安立、安住，达至一境，得入于定。诸比丘，比丘如是修习身至念。
evidence.english: “Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu acts with clear comprehension when going forward and returning; he acts with clear comprehension when looking ahead and looking around; he acts with clear comprehension when bending and stretching; he acts with clear comprehension when wearing his outer robe, bowl, and other robes; he acts with clear comprehension when eating, drinking, chewing, and tasting; he acts with clear comprehension when defecating and urinating; he acts with clear comprehension when walking, standing, sitting, sleeping, waking up, speaking, and keeping silent. As he dwells thus, diligent, ardent, and resolute, any thoughts connected with the household life are abandoned. With their abandonment, his mind becomes inwardly established, settles down, becomes unified, and concentrated. In this way too, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu develops mindfulness directed to the body.

entries.work_title: 分别论义注迷惑冰消 Sammohavinodanī-Aṭṭhakathā
entries.pali: So abhikkante…pe… tuṇhībhāve sampajānakārī hotī ti idamassa sabbattha satisampajaññasamannāgatattaparidīpanaṃ. So vivittaṃ senāsanaṃ bhajatī ti idamassa anurūpasenāsanapariggahaparidīpanaṃ. Araññaṃ…pe… paṭisallānasāruppa nti idamassa senāsanappabhedanirādīnavatānisaṃsaparidīpanaṃ. So araññagato vā ti idamassa vuttappakārena senāsanena yuttabhāvaparidīpanaṃ. Nisīdatī ti idamassa yogānurūpairiyāpathaparidīpanaṃ. Parimukhaṃ satiṃ upaṭṭhapetvā ti idamassa yogārambhaparidīpanaṃ. So abhijjhaṃ loke pahāyā tiādi panassa kammaṭṭhānānuyogena nīvaraṇappahānaparidīpanaṃ. Tasseva pahīnanīvaraṇassa vivicceva kāmehī tiādi paṭipāṭiyā jhānuppattiparidīpanaṃ.
entries.chinese_simplified: ‘彼于前进时……乃至……默然时，皆是正知而行’，此为阐明其于一切处皆具足念与正知。‘彼受用远离的坐卧处’，此为阐明其受用适宜的坐卧处。‘森林……乃至……适合独住’，此为阐明坐卧处的类别、无过患与利益。‘彼或往森林’，此为阐明其与如是所说之坐卧处相应。‘坐’，此为阐明适合禅修的威仪。‘于面前建立念’，此为阐明禅修的开始。‘彼于世间舍离贪欲’等，此为阐明通过致力于业处而舍断诸盖。‘对于已舍断诸盖的他，离诸欲’等，此为阐明禅那的次第生起。
entries.english: “When going forth… and so on… and being silent, he acts with clear comprehension”—this illuminates his being endowed with mindfulness and clear comprehension in all situations. “He resorts to a secluded dwelling”—this illuminates his choosing of a suitable dwelling. “The wilderness… and so on… suitable for seclusion”—this illuminates the classification, freedom from disadvantage, and advantages of dwellings. “Having gone to the wilderness, etc.”—this illuminates his being associated with a dwelling of the type described. “He sits down”—this illuminates his posture suitable for meditation. “Establishing mindfulness in front of him”—this illuminates the beginning of meditation. “Having abandoned covetousness for the world, etc.”—this illuminates his abandoning of the hindrances by application to the meditation subject. For one who has abandoned the hindrances, “secluded from sensual pleasures, etc.”—this illuminates the progressive arising of jhāna.

entries.work_title: 分别论义注迷惑冰消 Sammohavinodanī-Aṭṭhakathā
entries.pali: Sampajānakārī hotī ti sampajaññena sabbakiccakārī, sampajaññasseva vā kārī. So hi abhikkantādīsu sampajaññaṃ karoteva, na katthaci sampajaññavirahito hoti. Taṃ pana sampajaññaṃ yasmā satisampayuttameva hoti, tenassa niddese ‘‘sato sampajāno abhikkamati, sato sampajāno paṭikkamatī’’ti vuttaṃ.
entries.chinese_simplified: ‘有正知而行’(sampajānakārī hoti)是说以正知完成一切事务，或只是正知的行作者。因为他在前进等行为中确实保持正知，于任何处皆不离正知。又，此正知恒与念相应，故其解释中说：‘具念、正知而前进，具念、正知而后退’。
entries.english: ‘He acts with clear comprehension’ means he performs all activities with clear comprehension, or he is a doer of clear comprehension itself. For he indeed practices clear comprehension in going forward and so on, and is nowhere without clear comprehension. But since that clear comprehension is always associated with mindfulness, therefore in its explanation it is said: ‘Mindful and clearly comprehending, he goes forward; mindful and clearly comprehending, he returns.’

entries.work_title: 分别论义注迷惑冰消 Sammohavinodanī-Aṭṭhakathā
entries.pali: Niṭṭhito abhikkante paṭikkante sampajānakārī hotī tipadassa attho.
entries.chinese_simplified: ‘前进、后退时具正知者’此句之义已终。
entries.english: The meaning of the phrase 'one acts with clear comprehension when going forward and returning' is concluded.

entries.pali: Sammā pajānanaṃ sampajānaṃ, tena attanā kātabbakiccassa karaṇasīlo sampajānakārī ti āha ‘‘sampajaññena sabbakiccakārī’’ ti. Sampajānasaddassa sampajaññapariyāyatā pubbe vuttā eva. Sampajaññaṃ karotevā ti abhikkantādīsu asammohaṃ uppādeti eva. Sampajaññassa vā kāro etassa atthīti sampajānakārī. Dhammato vaḍḍhisaṅkhātena saha atthena vattatīti sātthakaṃ, abhikkantādi. Sātthakassa sampajānanaṃ sātthakasampajaññaṃ. Sappāyassa attano hitassa sampajānanaṃ sappāyasampajaññaṃ. Abhikkamādīsu bhikkhācāragocare, aññatthāpi ca pavattesu avijahite kammaṭṭhānasaṅkhāte gocare sampajaññaṃ gocarasampajaññaṃ. Abhikkamādīsu asammuyhanameva sampajaññaṃ asammohasampajaññaṃ. Pariggahetvā ti tūletvā tīretvā paṭisaṅkhāyāti, attho. Saṅghadassaneneva uposathapavāraṇādiatthaṃ gamanaṃ saṅgahitaṃ. Asubhadassanādī ti ādi -saddena kasiṇaparikammādīnaṃ saṅgaho daṭṭhabbo . Saṅkhepato vuttamatthaṃ vivarituṃ ‘‘cetiyaṃ vā bodhiṃ vā disvāpi hī’’ tiādi vuttaṃ. Arahattaṃ pāpuṇātī ti ukkaṭṭhaniddeso eso. Samathavipassanuppādanampi hi bhikkhuno vaḍḍhiyeva. Kecī ti abhayagirivāsino.
entries.chinese_simplified: 正确了知是为正知(sampajāna)，以此行持自身应作之事者，是为正知而行者(sampajānakārī)，因此说“以正知行一切事”。“正知”(sampajāna)一词是“正知”(sampajañña)的同义词，此点前已述。造作正知，即是在前进等活动中生起无痴。或者，此人有正知的造作，故为正知而行者。与从法增长之义俱行，故为有益(sātthaka)，如前进等。了知有益，即有益正知(sātthakasampajañña)。了知于己适宜有益，即适宜正知(sappāyasampajañña)。于前进等时，于托钵行境中，及于其他情况中，不舍弃被称为业处的行境，于此行境中的正知，即行境正知(gocarasampajañña)。于前进等时，不迷惑即是正知，即无痴正知(asammohasampajañña)。“抉择后”意即权衡、判断、省察后。仅以见僧即已摄入为布萨(uposatha)、自恣(pavāraṇā)等目的而去。于“见不净等”中，应知“等”字摄入遍作(kasiṇaparikamma)等。为解释前已略说之义，故说“即使见到塔庙或菩提树”等。“证得阿拉汉果”是最高的解释。比丘生起止(samatha)与观(vipassanā)亦是增长。所谓“一些人”是指无畏山(Abhayagiri)的住众。
entries.english: Rightly knowing is 'clear knowing' (sampajāna). One who is by nature a doer of a duty to be done by oneself with that is called 'one who acts with clear comprehension' (sampajānakārī), hence it is said, 'one who performs all duties with clear comprehension.' The fact that the word 'sampajāna' is a synonym for 'sampajañña' has indeed been stated previously. He indeed makes clear comprehension, that is, he indeed produces non-confusion in actions like going forward, etc. Alternatively, 'one who acts with clear comprehension' (sampajānakārī) means one who possesses the making of clear comprehension. It is 'meaningful' (sātthaka) because it proceeds with a benefit which is designated as growth in the Dhamma, as in going forward, etc. The clear comprehension of what is meaningful is 'meaningful clear comprehension' (sātthakasampajañña). The clear comprehension of what is suitable (sappāya), of one's own benefit, is 'suitable clear comprehension' (sappāyasampajañña). Clear comprehension in the sphere of a monk's conduct, such as going forward, etc., and in the field of alms-seeking, and in other activities where the meditation subject, which is designated as the domain (gocara), is not abandoned, is 'domain clear comprehension' (gocarasampajañña). Clear comprehension that is simply non-bewilderment in actions like going forward, etc., is 'non-bewilderment clear comprehension' (asammohasampajañña). 'Having grasped' (pariggahetvā) means having weighed, judged, and reflected upon—this is the meaning. Going for the purpose of the Uposatha or Pavāraṇā is included by the very seeing of the Saṅgha. 'Seeing the unattractive,' etc.—by the word 'etc.,' the inclusion of the preliminary work on kasiṇas, etc., should be understood. To explain the meaning stated briefly, 'for even having seen a shrine or a Bodhi tree,' etc., was stated. 'He attains Arahantship'—this is a statement of the highest. For a monk, the arising of serenity and insight is indeed growth. 'Some' refers to the dwellers at Abhayagiri.

entries.pali: Yasmā mahāsivattheravāde anantare anantare iriyāpathe pavattarūpārūpadhammānaṃ tattha tattheva nirodhadassanavasena sampajānakāritā gahitāti taṃ sampajaññavipassanācāravasena veditabbaṃ. Tena vuttaṃ ‘‘tayidaṃ mahāsivattherena vuttaṃ asammohadhuraṃ mahāsatipaṭṭhānasutte adhippeta’’ nti. Imasmiṃ pana sāmaññaphale sabbampi catubbidhaṃ sampajaññaṃ labbhati yāvadeva sāmaññaphalavisesadassanaparattā imissā desanāya. ‘‘Satisampayuttassevā’’ ti idaṃ yathā sampajaññassa kiccato padhānatā gahitā, evaṃ satiyā pīti dassanatthaṃ vuttaṃ, na satiyā sabbhāvamattadassanatthaṃ. Na hi kadāci satirahitā ñāṇappavatti atthi. ‘‘Etassa hi padassa ayaṃ vitthāro’’ ti iminā satiyā ñāṇena samadhurataṃyeva vibhāveti. Etāni padānī ti ‘‘abhikkante paṭikkante sampajānakārī hotī’’tiādīni padāni. Vibhattānevā ti visuṃ katvā vibhattāniyeva, imināpi sampajaññassa viya satiyāpettha padhānatameva vibhāveti.
entries.chinese_simplified: 在大希瓦(Mahāsiva)长老的学说中，正知而行，被理解为在每一个接续的威仪中，即于彼处，观见生起的色法与非色法之坏灭，故当知此为正知之观(vipassanā)行。是故说：‘此即大希瓦长老所说，为《大念处经》(Mahāsatipaṭṭhānasutta)所意指之不痴行。’然于此《沙门果经》(Sāmaññaphala Sutta)中，四种正知皆可得，因本经主旨在于开示沙门果之殊胜。‘唯与念相应者’一语，是为显示：正如正知于其作用上是主要的，念亦如是；而非仅为显示念之存在。盖无念之时，智识决不生起。‘此句之广说’，正阐明念与智(ñāṇa)同等重要。‘此等句’，即指‘前行、后退时，皆正知而行’等句。‘已分别说’，即已分别阐释，此亦阐明在此经中，念与正知同等重要。
entries.english: Because in the Mahāsivattheravāda, clear comprehension is taken as being active through seeing the cessation of material and immaterial phenomena arising in successive postures, then and there; therefore, it should be understood as conduct involving clear comprehension and insight. Hence it was said, “This was stated by the Mahāsivatthera as the burden of non-delusion, intended in the Great Discourse on the Foundations of Mindfulness.” But in this fruit of recluseship, all four kinds of clear comprehension are obtained, insofar as this teaching is for the purpose of showing the distinction of the fruit of recluseship. The phrase “only of one associated with mindfulness” is stated to show the pre-eminence of mindfulness by way of function, just as that of clear comprehension is taken as pre-eminent, and not to show merely the existence of mindfulness. For there is never any occurrence of knowledge devoid of mindfulness. “This is the detailed explanation of this term”: with this, it highlights that mindfulness and knowledge are of equal weight. “These terms”: that is, terms such as “one acts with clear comprehension when going forward, when going backward.” “Are distinctly analyzed”: meaning they are indeed analyzed by making them separate; even with this, it highlights that mindfulness, like clear comprehension, is pre-eminent here.

entries.pali: Majjhimabhāṇakā pana bhaṇanti – eko bhikkhu gacchanto aññaṃ cintento aññaṃ vitakkento gacchati, eko kammaṭṭhānaṃ avissajjetvāva gacchati. Tathā eko tiṭṭhanto…pe… nisīdanto…pe… sayanto aññaṃ cintento aññaṃ vitakkento sayati, eko kammaṭṭhānaṃ avissajjetvāva sayati, ettakena pana na pākaṭaṃ hotīti caṅkamanena dīpenti. Yo hi bhikkhu caṅkamaṃ otaritvā ca caṅkamanakoṭiyaṃ ṭhito pariggaṇhāti ‘‘pācīnacaṅkamanakoṭiyaṃ pavattā rūpārūpadhammā pacchimacaṅkamanakoṭiṃ appatvā ettheva niruddhā, pacchimacaṅkamanakoṭiyaṃ pavattāpi pācīnacaṅkamanakoṭiṃ appatvā ettheva niruddhā, caṅkamanamajjhe pavattā ubho koṭiyo appatvā ettheva niruddhā, caṅkamane pavattā rūpārūpadhammā ṭhānaṃ appatvā ettheva niruddhā, ṭhāne pavattā nisajjaṃ appatvā ettheva niruddhā, nisajjāya pavattā sayanaṃ appatvā ettheva niruddhā’’ti evaṃ pariggaṇhanto pariggaṇhantoyeva bhavaṅgaṃ otarati. Uṭṭhahanto kammaṭṭhānaṃ gahetvāva uṭṭhahati, ayaṃ bhikkhu gatādīsu sampajānakārī nāma hotīti . Evampi na sotte kammaṭṭhānaṃ avibhūtaṃ hoti, tasmā bhikkhu yāva sakkoti, tāva caṅkamitvā ṭhatvā nisīditvā sayamāno evaṃ pariggahetvā sayati ‘‘kāyo acetano, mañco acetano, kāyo na jānāti ‘ahaṃ mañce sayito’ti, mañco na jānāti ‘mayi kāyo sayito’ti, acetano kāyo acetane mañce sayito’’ti evaṃ pariggaṇhanto eva cittaṃ bhavaṅge otāreti. Pabujjhanto kammaṭṭhānaṃ gahetvāva pabujjhati, ayaṃ sotte sampajānakārī nāma hoti. Kāyādīkiriyānibbattanena tammayattā, āvajjanakiriyā samuṭṭhitattā ca javanaṃ sabbampi vā chadvārappavattaṃ kiriyamayapavattaṃ nāma. Tasmiṃ sati jāgaritaṃ nāma hotīti pariggaṇhanto jāgarite sampajānakārī nāma. Api ca rattindivaṃ cha koṭṭhāse katvā pañca koṭṭhāse jaggantopi jāgarite sampajānakārī nāma hoti. Vimuttāyatanasīsena dhammaṃ desentopi battiṃsatiracchānakathaṃ pahāya dasakathāvatthunissitasappāyakathaṃ kathentopi bhāsite sampajānakārī nāma. Aṭṭhatiṃsāya ārammaṇesu cittaruciyaṃ manasikāraṃ pavattentopi dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ samāpannopi tuṇhībhāve sampajānakārī nāma. Dutiyañhi jhānaṃ vacīsaṅkhāravirahato visesato tuṇhībhāvo nāmāti. Eva nti vuttappakārena, sattasupi ṭhānesu catudhāti attho.
entries.chinese_simplified: 中部诵者(Majjhimabhāṇakā)则说：一比丘行走时，心缘余处，思惟余事而行；另一比丘则不舍业处而行。同样，站立时……乃至……坐时……乃至……卧时，心缘余处，思惟余事而卧；另一比丘则不舍业处而卧。然仅此说尚不显了，故以经行明之。若有比丘，下至经行处，立于经行道一端，当如是把握：‘于东边经行道生起的色、非色法，未至西边经行道，即于此处灭；于西边经行道生起的，未至东边经行道，亦于此处灭；于经行道中途生起的，未至两端，亦于此处灭。于经行时生起的色、非色法，未至站立，即于此处灭；于站立时生起的，未至坐，即于此处灭；于坐时生起的，未至卧，即于此处灭。’如是把握时，心即入有分(bhavaṅga)。起身时，亦执持业处而起，此比丘名为‘于往来等有正知者’。即使如此，于睡眠中业处也不会变得不明显。是故比丘应尽力经行、站立、坐、卧，并如是把握而入睡：‘身无心，床亦无心。身不知“我卧于床”，床亦不知“身卧我上”。无心之身卧于无心之床上。’如是把握时，心即入有分。醒觉时，亦执持业处而醒，此名为‘于睡眠有正知者’。由于成就了身体等行为，与之一致，且由作意行为而生起，故一切速行，或说于六门转起者，皆名为‘唯作转起’。当此存在时，名为‘醒觉’。如此了知者，名为‘于醒觉有正知者’。复次，将一日夜分为六分，醒觉五分者，亦名为‘于醒觉有正知者’。以解脱处为题说法，舍离三十二种畜生论(tiracchānakathā)，宣说依于十论事的适宜之论者，名为‘于言语有正知者’。于三十八所缘中，随心所乐而起作意者，乃至入第二禅定者，名为‘于默然有正知者’。因为第二禅尤其无有语行，故名为‘默然’。意思是：如是，依所说之方式，于此七处皆有四种（正知）。
entries.english: The Middle Reciters, however, say: One monk walks while thinking one thing and pondering another, while another walks without abandoning his meditation subject. Similarly, one stands… sits… lies down while thinking one thing and pondering another, while another lies down without abandoning his meditation subject. But by this much it is not made clear, so they explain it by way of walking meditation. For a monk who, having entered the walking path and standing at the end of it, comprehends thus: “The material and immaterial phenomena that arise at the eastern end of the walking path cease right there without reaching the western end. Those that arise at the western end also cease right there without reaching the eastern end. Those that arise in the middle cease right there without reaching either end. The material and immaterial phenomena that arise while walking cease right there without reaching the standing posture. Those that arise while standing cease right there without reaching the sitting posture. Those that arise while sitting cease right there without reaching the lying down posture.” While comprehending thus, he sinks into the life-continuum. When rising, he rises only after taking up his meditation subject. Such a monk is called one who acts with clear comprehension in going, and so forth. Even so, the meditation subject is not indistinct while sleeping. Therefore, a monk, for as long as he is able, having walked, stood, and sat, should lie down after comprehending thus: “The body is without consciousness; the bed is without consciousness. The body does not know, ‘I am lying on the bed,’ nor does the bed know, ‘The body is lying on me.’ A body without consciousness lies on a bed without consciousness.” While comprehending thus, he lets his mind sink into the life-continuum. When waking, he wakes only after taking up his meditation subject. Such a one is called one who acts with clear comprehension in sleep. Because it is constituted by the performance of bodily and other actions, and because it arises from the act of adverting, all impulsion (javana), or that which occurs through the six doors, is called a process composed of action. When this is present, it is called wakefulness. One who comprehends thus is called one who acts with clear comprehension in wakefulness. Moreover, one who stays awake for five out of the six portions of the day and night is also called one who acts with clear comprehension in wakefulness. One who teaches the Dhamma with the principle of the bases of liberation, abandoning the thirty-two kinds of worldly talk and speaking only on suitable topics based on the ten subjects of discussion, is called one who acts with clear comprehension in speech. One who directs attention to one of the thirty-eight objects according to the mind’s preference, or one who has attained the second jhāna, is called one who acts with clear comprehension in silence. For the second jhāna is especially called silence because it is free from verbal formations. Thus, in the manner stated, the meaning is fourfold in all seven instances.

entries.pali: 557-558 . Yassa adhigatattā arahato pariññeyyādīsu anavasesato sammoho vigato, taṃ aggamaggañāṇaṃ sandhāya ‘‘maggañāṇassā’’ ti vadanti. Yasmā tassa sabbassa satokāritā viya sampajānakāritā, tasmā tena ñāṇena so ñāṇī. Satipaññāvepullappatto hi so uttamapuriso.
entries.chinese_simplified: 557-558. 由于阿罗汉(arahat)已证得此智，对‘应遍知’(pariññeyya)等法已毫无遗余地离除了痴迷(sammoha)，故针对那最上道智(aggamaggañāṇa)而说‘道智的’。由于他的一切行为都像是有念(sati)而为，也有正知(sampajañña)而为，因此他因那智慧而为具智者。因为那位最上士(uttamapurisa)确实已达到念与慧的圆满。
entries.english: 557-558. The term 'of path knowledge' refers to the supreme path knowledge, due to the attainment of which all delusion regarding what should be fully understood, etc., is completely eradicated in an Arahant. Because for him, everything is done with clear comprehension as if with mindfulness, therefore, by that knowledge, he is a 'knower'. For that supreme person has attained the abundance of mindfulness and wisdom.

entries.pali: So abhikkante paṭikkante sampajānakārī hoti, ālokite vilokite sampajānakārī hoti, samiñjite pasārite sampajānakārī hoti, saṅghāṭipattacīvaradhāraṇe sampajānakārī hoti, asite pīte khāyite sāyite sampajānakārī hoti, uccārapassāvakamme sampajānakārī hoti, gate ṭhite nisinne sutte jāgarite bhāsite tuṇhībhāve sampajānakārī hoti.
entries.chinese_simplified: 他前进后退时保持正知，瞻视、环顾时保持正知，屈伸时保持正知，穿着僧伽梨、受持衣钵时保持正知，食、饮、嚼、尝时保持正知，大小便时保持正知，行、住、坐、卧、醒、语、默时，皆保持正知。
entries.english: He is one who acts with clear comprehension when going forward and returning; when looking ahead and looking around; when bending and stretching his limbs; when carrying his outer robe, bowl, and robes; when eating, drinking, consuming food, and tasting; when defecating and urinating; and when walking, standing, sitting, falling asleep, waking up, speaking, and keeping silent.

entries.pali: Idāni taṃ jāgariyānuyogaṃ sarūpato dassento ‘‘bodhipakkhikānaṃ dhammāna’’ ntiādimāha. Bodhipakkhikānaṃ dhammāna nti catusaccāvabodhasaṅkhātassa maggañāṇassa pakkhe bhavānaṃ catusaccasatipaṭṭhānādisattatiṃsadhammānaṃ. Niddese panassa lokiyabhāvanāya visesabodhipakkhiyadhamme ekārammaṇe pavattanasamatthatāya satta bojjhaṅgā eva niddiṭṭhā. Tesaṃ gahaṇena pana sesānampi tattha gahaṇaṃ veditabbaṃ. So abhikkante paṭikkante tiādīsu abhikkantaṃ vuccati purato gamanaṃ, paṭikkantaṃ nivattanaṃ, tadubhayañca ṭhānanisajjāsayanesupi purato, pacchato ca kāyassa abhigamanaapagamanavasena labbhati. Sampajānakārī hotī ti sampajaññena sabbakiccakārī, sampajaññasseva vā kārī, sampajañña-ggahaṇena cettha avippayogato satipi gahitāva hoti. Tenevassa niddese ‘‘sato sampajāno abhikkamatī’’tiādi vuttaṃ.
entries.chinese_simplified: 现在为了如实地说明该警寤勤修，（论师）说‘菩提分法’等。所谓菩提分法，是指能帮助证悟四圣谛之道智的助伴，即四念处等三十七法。但在其解释(niddesa)中，只提到了七觉支，因为它们能在世间修习中专注于单一所缘，从而变得殊胜。通过理解这七觉支，也应明白其余的法也包含在内。在‘前进、后退’等（词语）中，‘前进’是指向前走，‘后退’是指后退。这两种动作，无论在站立、坐卧时，都可以通过身体向前或向后的移动而实现。‘正知而作’是指以正知完成所有事情，或者说专注于正知。在此处提到‘正知’，实际上由于正知与正念不分离，因此也包含了正念。因此，在其解释中才会说‘具念正知地前进’等等。
entries.english: Now, showing that practice of wakefulness in its own nature, he states the passage beginning 'of the things pertaining to enlightenment.' 'Of the things pertaining to enlightenment' means of the thirty-seven things—such as the four establishments of mindfulness and so on—that are on the side of the path knowledge which is the awakening to the four truths. However, in the Exposition of this, only the seven enlightenment factors are pointed out, as they are the special things pertaining to enlightenment in mundane development, because of their ability to proceed on a single object. But by their inclusion, the inclusion of the rest there should also be understood. In 'in going forward, in returning,' etc., 'going forward' is called going ahead; 'returning' is turning back. And both are found in standing, sitting, and lying down, by way of the body's moving towards and moving away, forwards and backwards. 'He acts with clear comprehension' means he is one who does all actions with clear comprehension, or one who is a doer of clear comprehension itself. And here, by the inclusion of clear comprehension, mindfulness too is included because of its inseparability. For that reason, in its Exposition it is said: 'Mindful and clearly comprehending, he goes forward,' and so on.
